expectations.text: Acceptance criteria use user-observable EARS format
expectations.evidence: Acceptance criteria use EARS patterns such as "WHEN I open the settings page THEN I SHALL see a clear option to switch between light and dark appearance", "IF I have not changed appearance settings before THEN I SHALL see a sensible default appearance", and "WHILE dark mode is active THE USER SHALL be able to read all labels, controls, and status messages".

expectations.text: No API endpoints or database schemas in acceptance criteria
expectations.evidence: Acceptance criteria describe only user-visible outcomes (appearance options, color scheme changes, persistence, legibility) with no mention of APIs, endpoints, databases, or schemas.

expectations.text: Includes As a / I want / so that structure
expectations.evidence: User Story section includes: "As a Night Shift Professional", "I want to enable dark mode from the settings page", and "so that I can view and change my preferences comfortably in low-light conditions without unnecessary eye strain".
